issues.claim: Collection rules consist of a trigger (...), actions (`CollectTrace`, `CollectDump`) and limits (`ActionCount` per `ActionCountSlidingWindowDuration`)
issues.problem: The names are correct from my knowledge of dotnet-monitor: triggers such as EventCounter, AspNetRequestDuration and AspNetResponseStatus; actions CollectTrace and CollectDump; limits ActionCount and ActionCountSlidingWindowDuration; egress providers. None of the fetched excerpts shows them. The Learn page excerpt only says 'automated rules', and the repo root page only mentions triggers in general. The third link is the repo root, not a documentation page.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally replace the repo-root link with the collection-rules configuration page in the dotnet-monitor repo (documentation/configuration/collection-rules-configuration.md), so a reader can check these names.

issues.claim: It reaches the process through the diagnostic port, so the application image needs no diagnostic tools.
issues.problem: This is correct in outline. In the default connect mode, the sidecar and the app share a volume holding the diagnostic socket (usually /tmp). The `--diagnostic-port` option in the excerpt is for listen mode. The text does not mention the shared volume, which is the practical condition for the sidecar to work.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'It reaches the process through the runtime diagnostic channel (a Unix domain socket on a shared volume in connect mode, or the diagnostic port in listen mode), so the application image needs no diagnostic tools.' Make the same change in the ru text.

issues.claim: `System.Text.Json` по умолчанию пропускает неизвестные свойства JSON, а свойство, которого нет в JSON, оставляет со значением по умолчанию (исключение будет только для членов `required`)
issues.problem: The cited page, 'Handle unmapped members', supports only the first half: unknown JSON properties are ignored by default. Defaults for properties missing from the JSON and the exception for `required` members are documented on the required-properties page. The claim itself is correct (.NET 7+).
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/required-properties (kind docs) with a linkTitle in both locales, or soften the sentence to what the cited page shows.

issues.claim: `BinaryFormatter` was removed in .NET 9, so a cache full of such payloads becomes unreadable as a whole after the upgrade.
issues.problem: The migration guide says the implementation is no longer included in the runtime, and the APIs remain but always throw PlatformNotSupportedException. 'Removed' is imprecise. Readability can be restored only through the unsupported System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters package.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'the BinaryFormatter implementation was removed in .NET 9 (its methods throw PlatformNotSupportedException), so such payloads become unreadable after the upgrade'. Make the same change in the ru text.

issues.problem: `AddSerializer<T, TImplementation>()` does exist on the HybridCache builder, but the fetched HybridCache excerpt shows only `AddSerializerFactory`, so the name is unconfirmed by the excerpt. `AddSerializer` is per type, while `AddSerializerFactory` covers many types.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'registered with `AddSerializer<T, TImpl>()` or `AddSerializerFactory<T>()`'. Make the same change in the ru text.
